data.narrative:
Axelera AI, a Series C-stage chip design company, is evaluated against a peer set of 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-tech firms in the same sector, with particular focus on 5 near-peer private companies including Etched ($5.0B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and DEEPX ($529M).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression anchors to the company's $450M total raised as a proxy for current value, applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, yielding $765M. Peer-median valuation uses the 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables listed above, which span a range of $529M to $5.0B with a median of $2.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 21.4x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not provide.

The triangulated analysis across the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $650M to $2.3B, with a median implied value of $1.4B. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the peer median—driven significantly by Etched's outlier $5.0B valuation—and the absence of revenue or profitability data to calibrate relative to public comparables. The wide peer range ($529M–$5.0B) reflects genuine heterogeneity in stage and traction within the frontier-chip sector.
